stem:
The compound chlorine dioxide, $\text{ClO}_2$, can be prepared by the reaction shown.

$$\text{NaClO}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{ClO}_2 + \text{NaCl}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Using oxidation numbers, explain why this reaction is a redox reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The central atom in the molecule of $\text{ClO}_2$ is chlorine.

Draw the 'dot-and-cross' diagram for $\text{ClO}_2$. Show outer electrons only.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The reaction between $\text{ClO}_2$ and $\text{F}_2$ is shown.

$$2\text{ClO}_2 + \text{F}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{ClO}_2\text{F}$$

The rate of the reaction was measured at various concentrations of the two reactants and the following results were obtained.

| experiment | $[\text{ClO}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{F}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate $/\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $0.010$ | $0.060$ | $2.20 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 2 | $0.025$ | $0.060$ | to be calculated |
| 3 | to be calculated | $0.040$ | $7.04 \times 10^{-3}$ |

The rate equation is rate = $k[\text{ClO}_2][\text{F}_2]$.
parts.text: What is meant by the term order of reaction with respect to a particular reagent?

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use the results of experiment 1 to calculate the rate constant, $k$, for this reaction. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Use the data in the table to calculate

- the initial rate in experiment 2,

- $[\text{ClO}_2]$ in experiment 3.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: What is meant by the term rate-determining step?

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The equation for the reaction between $\text{ClO}_2$ and $\text{F}_2$ is shown.

$$2\text{ClO}_2 + \text{F}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{ClO}_2\text{F}$$

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{ClO}_2][\text{F}_2]$$

The mechanism for this reaction has two steps.

Suggest equations for the **two** steps of this mechanism, stating which of the two steps is the rate-determining step.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: By considering the rate equation, explain why the rate increases with increasing temperature.
